To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

health literacy and numeracy are important determinants of understanding graphical risk estimates, that the relationship is not linear, and that health literacy is the most important determinant of risk interpretation.

(1) Health literacy is a strong predictor of the understanding of breast cancer risk estimates presented as a number, a graph, or a table; (2) Numeracy is a strong predictor for the understanding of breast risk presented as a number; and (3) Health literacy and numeracy are strong predictors of the ability to understand the meaning of the risk estimates presented as tables and graphs.
the use of graphical risk estimates in the context of health literacy, numeracy and interpretation can be a powerful tool for communicating risk information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a theory of health literacy that will help to improve the health of populations.
how people make sense of risk estimates in the context of health literacy, numeracy and graphical displays of information.
the role of the media, the role of the public, and how these two entities interact in the process of risk communication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the health literacy of the general population is low, and that health literacy levels are associated with health status, health behaviors, and access to and utilization of healthcare.
the use of a single risk estimate for a woman's lifetime breast cancer risk is not a useful tool for communicating breast cancer risk.
the use of the Internet has had an overall positive impact on health literacy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the health care system is a complex system and it is important to understand how the system works in order to make it more efficient, effective, and equitable.
the results of the study are not in support of the idea that the use of graphical displays in the context of health information is a panacea.
we have shown that there is a strong link between health literacy and health outcomes and that there are many factors that influence the relationship.
The main takeaway from our work is that
health literacy is a significant predictor of the interpretation of graphical risk estimates.
the majority of women in our study were unable to accurately interpret graphical breast cancer risk information.
health literacy is an important factor to consider when designing and implementing risk communication strategies.
